title: A provider that rejoins a room records a false gap
description:
Found while answering whether jump detection belongs in an I-D
(2026-11-25).

## Why jump detection is sound at all

The fanout sequence is per ROOM and one per event
(store/log.rs::next_fanout_seq, "every row of one fanout carries the
same sequence"), while delivery is per DESTINATION (room_fanout is keyed
on domain, because a handshake fanout's BYTES differ per destination).

So a destination's numbers are contiguous only because every fanout of a
room goes to every provider then in it: hub/update.rs builds
`destinations` as the union of the domains before and after, plus the
sender, and hub/submit.rs as every member domain. The bytes differ per
destination; the set of destinations does not.

That is an accident of the implementation, not a stated rule. See the
I-D note below.

## The bug

A provider that leaves a room and rejoins later sees a legitimate jump:

- it is in the room to sequence 10, so highest_fanout_seq = 10;
- it leaves; the room runs on to 49 without it;
- it rejoins and receives sequence 50.

50 > 10 + 1, so note_position records gap_from = 11. But 11..49 is not
missing: this provider was not in the room and is not entitled to it
(docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §8). fill_gap then asks, the hub's §8 bound
serves nothing, the gap never clears, and a 410 would mark it unfillable
and resync every client of that provider for data it should never have
had.

"First fanout is never a gap" does not cover this: it is not the first
fanout for the room, only the first since rejoining.

## Fix, roughly

On being added to a room again, the follower's position should be reset
rather than continued -- its highest should become the sequence at which
it rejoined, with no gap. The join is already visible on the follower
side (`follower_member`, and Follower::accept_fanout's membership
handling), so the information is there.

Needs a test: leave at 10, rejoin at 50, assert no gap is recorded.

## For the I-D

Two properties that catch-up's local half depends on, which a draft must
state or another implementation can break silently:

1. every fanout of a room goes to every provider then in the room, so a
   destination's received sequences are contiguous. Without it, jump
   detection produces false gaps on every implementation that fans out
   to a subset.
2. a hub serves catch-up contiguously from `from`, for that requester.
   Follower::fill_gap relies on this to know the gap is closed (its
   `target`), and the reliance is documented in its rustdoc.

Jump detection and the fill loop themselves are local policy and should
NOT be normative: a follower may notice a gap however it likes, or only
probe (decision mimid-1wgh.37.104.11).
